title: Rigatoni with Meat Sauce
seoTitle: Rigatoni with Meat Sauce | Firefighter Meal
shortDescription: Slow-simmered beef and pork ragù over rigatoni for ten
subtitle: Slow-simmered beef and pork ragù over rigatoni for ten
description: Ground beef and pork simmer with onion, garlic, and crushed tomatoes until thick and rich. Toss with rigatoni and finish with Parmesan for a proper Italian-American hall feed.

steps.title: Gather ingredients and equipment
steps.instruction: Line up every ingredient for Rigatoni with Meat Sauce in the order you will cook — measure spices into ramekins, trim proteins on a dedicated board, and set tongs, thermometers, and hotel pans within arm's reach before any heat goes on.

steps.title: Preheat ovens and surfaces
steps.instruction: Preheat ovens, griddles, or grills to recipe temp before the crew arrives — cold equipment extends cook time and dries out batch beef. Confirm burners ignite evenly and sheet pans are greased or lined.

steps.title: Brown the meats
steps.instruction: Cook beef and pork with onion over medium-high heat 12–15 minutes, breaking into crumbles until well browned. Drain excess fat. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

steps.title: Build the sauce
steps.instruction: Add garlic and tomato paste, cook 2 minutes. Pour in wine and simmer until mostly reduced, about 4 minutes. Maintain a steady simmer — bubbles should break the surface without a rolling boil that shreds delicate proteins. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

steps.title: Simmer low
steps.instruction: Add crushed tomatoes and oregano. Simmer uncovered 40–45 minutes, stirring occasionally, until sauce thickens and oil pools at edges.

steps.title: Cook rigatoni
steps.instruction: Boil rigatoni in salted water until al dente, about 11 minutes. Drain and toss with a cup of sauce. Maintain a steady simmer — bubbles should break the surface without a rolling boil that shreds delicate proteins. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

steps.title: Verify safe internal temps
steps.instruction: Spot-check the thickest pieces with an instant-read thermometer — target 145°F for medium beef, 160°F for ground. If any piece reads low, return it to heat immediately rather than holding under temp on the line.

steps.title: Hold for call interruptions
steps.instruction: If tones drop mid-service, cover finished food and hold at 140°F in a warm cabinet or 200°F oven — never leave proteins below 140°F for more than 30 minutes cumulative. Note the hold time on the pan with a grease pencil.

steps.title: Serve family-style
steps.instruction: Portion pasta into bowls or hotel pan, top with remaining sauce and Parmesan. Serve with extra cheese at the line. Plan about 5 minutes for this step at crew scale. Keep a backup tray at 200°F for firefighters returning from a call — never serve picked-over pans to late crew. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

proTips: A parmesan rind simmered in the sauce adds savory depth—fish it out before serving.
Red pepper flake pinch in the browning stage wakes up canned tomatoes.
Double the batch and freeze half sauce for an emergency pasta night.
tonightSpread: Rigatoni with meat sauce, garlic bread, and simple green salad.
Roasted zucchini on the side for crew who want vegetables.
leftovers: Bake into a pasta casserole with extra mozzarella on top.
Stuff into hoagie rolls with melted provolone for meatball-less subs.
whyCrewsLikeIt: Meat sauce is the pasta baseline everyone recognizes. It scales cheap, simmers while you handle other duties, and holds hot in a hotel pan for late eaters.
mealPrepNotes: Simmer sauce at least 45 minutes for depth—longer is better. Salt pasta water heavily. Sauce and pasta can stay separate until service if holding.
